# Symphony + Claude Lane

> A portable skill for adding a specialized Claude Code lane to an existing OpenAI Symphony + Linear workflow.

## What this repo is

This repo teaches an agent how to introduce a Claude lane into a mixed-lane delivery system where Symphony handles worker orchestration and Linear holds issue planning and state.

The default Claude lane is intentionally narrow:

- UI and UX implementation that benefits from visual judgment
- browser-verified frontend changes
- product copy and higher-touch writing
- review-oriented or skeptical follow-up work

The skill also teaches the agent to ask the adopter whether Claude should own any additional areas, then persist those answers into a repo-local routing profile.
If the adopter does not answer, the skill keeps Claude narrow and records that assumption explicitly.
The routing profile also captures queue strategy, inherited guardrails, privacy rules, and cleanup or retention rules so the lane accounts for that adopter's actual storage footprint, including worktrees, snapshots, and any repo-specific hotspots.

## Default workflow

Inspect repo -> confirm mixed-lane candidate -> confirm the base Symphony workflow already has bootstrap assertions and a no-progress stop-loss -> ask adopter what Claude should own -> fall back to UI-first if unanswered -> create or update `.orchestration/claude-lane.yaml` including queue strategy, privacy rules, and retention policy -> prefer same-project label routing unless stronger separation is needed -> document lane contract -> use Playwright for visual verification -> apply safe closeout and cleanup rules

## Repo structure

- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/SKILL.md` — main skill definition
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/agents/openai.yaml` — skill UI metadata
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/references/setup.md` — prerequisites and candidate checks
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/references/routing.md` — routing defaults, extension questions, persisted profile contract
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/references/dispatch.md` — queue split, separate Claude project, worker lifecycle
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/references/visual-verification.md` — Playwright-first browser verification guidance
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/references/closeout.md` — outcome blocks, `In Review`, retries, self-close rules
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/references/troubleshooting.md` — common mixed-lane failure modes
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/references/examples.md` — concrete ticket-routing examples
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/assets/claude-lane-profile.example.yaml` — example routing profile and cleanup policy adopters should copy into their repo
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/assets/claude-lane-guidance.snippet.md` — starter guidance adopters can drop into repo-local docs
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/assets/worker-prompt.template.md` — reusable worker prompt template
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/assets/linear-outcome-block.example.md` — example structured closeout comments

## Usage

Install the skill into Codex or point Claude Code at `skills/symphony-claude-lane/SKILL.md`. Then ask the agent to add a Claude lane to a Symphony + Linear repo, keeping the default lane UI-first unless the adopter wants Claude to own more.

## What this repo does not include

No machine-specific launcher scripts, no env wrappers, no watchdog, and no universal worker runtime. This is a portable blueprint meant to be adapted into local orchestration stacks, with safe defaults for closeout and cleanup when tracker state is unavailable.
